stories.headline: Cyclone looms, but wait for widespread rain continues in Tamil Nadu
stories.title: Cyclone looms, but wait for widespread rain continues in Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: Weather system to bring isolated heavy rainfall over a few north coastal districts; November rain most likely to be below normal in T.N., says IMD
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Bay of Bengal is churning its next cyclonic storm.
After the powerful Cyclone Arnab that made landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast, the depression over southeast Bay of Bengal is likely to become a severe cyclonic storm by Sunday.
The weather system is likely to reach westcentral Bay of Bengal near south Andhra Pradesh by the early hours of Tuesday.
Tamil Nadu, however, may have to wait for its turn of widespread rainfall until November 8.
The new weather system would bring isolated heavy rainfall over a few north coastal districts — Cuddalore, Tiruvallur and Villupuram — between Monday and Tuesday.
Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast that November rainfall is most likely to be below normal in Tamil Nadu.
Rainfall over the entire southern peninsula is likely to be around only 77% of the long period average of 118.7 mm.

Addressing a virtual media briefing on Saturday, IMD Director-General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said southern States, including Tamil Nadu, are likely to experience above normal maximum and minimum temperatures in November.
He noted that very strong El Nino conditions are likely to prevail during November and December.
Tamil Nadu ended October with a 27% rainfall surplus despite a prolonged dry spell that had shrunk monsoon surplus.
Rainfall over the monsoon core zones in southern States this October was the ninth lowest since 2001, according to the IMD.

V.R. Durai, Head, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, RMC, said that with Cyclone Arnab losing its strength, northeasterly winds are gradually returning to Tamil Nadu and this would bring light to moderate rainfall, particularly over north Tamil Nadu and interior districts till November 3.

stories.headline: Naidu calls for high alert as another cyclone threat looms over Andhra Pradesh
stories.title: Naidu calls for high alert as another cyclone threat looms over Andhra Pradesh
stories.summary: Depression over southeast Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into a cyclone by November 1; officials told to monitor its movement every six hours and expedite restoration works in cyclone-hit areas
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to expedite restoration works in the areas affected by Cyclone Arnab and called for a high alert in view of the threat of another cyclone.

With a depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal predicted to intensify into a cyclone by November 1, moderate to heavy rainfall is likely in the south coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema regions on November 2, 3 and 4.
Mr. Naidu stressed the need for precautionary measures to minimise the impact.

Reviewing relief and restoration measures in the cyclone-hit districts at the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) Centre in the Secretariat on Saturday, he directed officials to monitor the movement of the depression every six hours using satellite imagery and Doppler radars and take appropriate measures based on its trajectory.
He also called for efficient utilisation of rainwater, uninterrupted mobile phone connectivity and the maximum possible use of battery energy storage systems.
Officials informed him that power restoration works were progressing at a brisk pace in the affected areas, with 7,000 personnel and 400 machines deployed.

Mr. Naidu directed officials to urgently restore the protection wall at Kakinada, clear silt from canals in the Narsapuram and Katrenikona areas, and strengthen drainage systems in Konaseema and West Godavari districts to ensure the smooth flow of water.
He called for steps to extend insurance coverage to all farmers from the next agricultural season and stressed the need to promote natural farming.
The Chief Minister ordered compensation of ₹54,000 per hectare for damage to 1,293 hectares of coconut plantations and ₹1,500 for each uprooted coconut tree.
Officials informed him that about 1.95 lakh coconut trees had been damaged.
They also said steps were being taken to pay compensation of ₹35,000 per hectare for banana crop losses across 15,000 hectares.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab: Odisha floods ease in Ganjam, Gajapati as relief intensifies
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: Odisha floods ease in Ganjam, Gajapati as relief intensifies
stories.summary: Cyclone Arnab: Odisha floods ease in Ganjam, Gajapati as relief intensifies
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Floodwaters receded in cyclone-hit Ganjam and Gajapati as officials accelerated relief and restoration work.
Falling river levels have reduced immediate danger, but waterlogging and infrastructure repairs persist.

The flood situation in Odisha's cyclone-hit Ganjam and Gajapati districts improved gradually on Saturday as water receded from most affected areas and river levels declined, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi directed officials to step up relief and restoration work.
Ganjam and Gajapati were the worst affected among the nine southern districts hit by very severe Cyclone Arnab.
More than 1.5 lakh people were affected in Ganjam and over 30,000 in Gajapati, prompting the authorities to evacuate residents and open relief camps.
Ganjam Collector V Keerthi Vasan told PTI that 56,051 people had been moved to 367 safe shelters, while cooked food was being distributed at 370 locations across the district.
Around 700 people remained stranded in waterlogged areas, he said.
Food had been delivered by air to cut-off villages using Indian Navy and Indian Coast Guard helicopters.
Adequate food stocks were being maintained to meet requirements for the next 15 to 20 days.
The number of cut-off villages in Ganjam fell from 70 on Thursday to 21 on Friday and three on Saturday.
Vasan said schools in the district would remain closed until November 3 because of flooding and waterlogging.

stories.headline: IOA’s election Code of Conduct bars criticism of ‘private life’ of candidates, publicity
stories.title: IOA’s election Code of Conduct bars criticism of ‘private life’ of candidates, publicity
stories.summary: The election to pick 10 members of the Athletes' Commission of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) will be held on November 3, while the polls to choose eight SOMs will be held on November 9
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: No criticism of opponents’ “private lives”, a bar on all forms of publicity, including the use of new media and social networks, and a requirement for IOA and NSF office-bearers to maintain neutrality feature in the Model Code of Conduct for the upcoming elections to the Athletes’ Commission and Sportspersons of Merit (SOMs).
The election to pick 10 members of the Athletes' Commission of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) will be held on November 3, while the polls to choose eight SOMs will be held on November 9.
Both elections will be held virtually, and separate instructions will be issued later by Electoral Officer Sanjay Kumar Srivastava.
There are 12 candidates — including Olympic medallists P.V. Sindhu and Mirabai Chanu — in the fray for the Athletes' Commission membership.
The 10 members — five men and five women — will be elected by the 34 members of the electoral college — two each from 17 National Sports Federations (NSFs).
Eight SOMs — four men and four women — will be elected from among 80 SOMs — 40 men and 40 women — notified by the Electoral Officer.
Some of the legendary figures of Indian sports, including incumbent IOA President P.T. Usha, are in the fray to become one of the eight SOMs.

"A candidate shall not produce any spoken word, written text or representation of any nature likely to harm the image of another candidate or cause him prejudice, and criticism of other candidates, if made, shall be confined to their policies and programme, past record and work," one of the provisions of the Model Code of Conduct said.

"The promotion of a candidate shall exclude any form of publicity, including the use of new media or social networks, and no public meeting or gathering of any kind may be organised in the process of promoting a candidature.”
"NSF and candidates shall refrain from criticism of all aspects of private life, not connected with the public activities of the athletes.
No candidate shall engage in criticism based on unverified allegations or distortion against any other candidate, and there shall be no appeal to caste or communal feelings for securing votes."
The Model Code of Conduct also prescribed that electoral campaigns shall be carried out by the candidates in a fair manner and, in a spirit of respect for fundamental ethical principles.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves site for Uppara community hall in Kalaburagi
stories.title: Cabinet approves site for Uppara community hall in Kalaburagi
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Karnataka Cabinet has approved the allotment of a civic amenity (CA) site at Kusanur village in Kalaburagi for the construction of a community hall for the Uppara community, fulfilling a long-pending demand of the community.
In a media note released on Friday, Minister Priyank Kharge announced that the Cabinet, chaired by the Chief Minister, had decided to allot the site to the district Uppara Sangha.
The site, measuring 439.67 sq.
and bearing the number PL-01, is located in Survey No. 19/2B at Kusanur village.
It is a civic amenity site in a private layout approved by the Kalaburagi Urban Development Authority.
Mr. Kharge said the allotment would benefit members of the Uppara community, which he described as socially, educationally and economically disadvantaged.
The proposed community hall would provide a venue for community activities and cultural programmes, contributing to the welfare and development of the community.

stories.headline: Sebi bars EKI Energy, MD Dabkara, others from market; imposes penalty
stories.title: Sebi bars EKI Energy, MD Dabkara, others from market; imposes penalty
stories.summary: Markets regulator Sebi has barred EKI Energy Services Ltd and its Managing Director Manish Kumar Dabkara from the securities market for two months and 12 months, respectively, for misrepresenting financial statements of the carbon credits trading firm and diverting funds. Also, the regulator has restrained the company's former Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Mohit Kumar Agarwal from the securities market for eight months, while whole-time directors Naveen Sharma and Sonali Sheikh have been prohibited for five months and one month, respectively. Besides, Sebi has imposed monetary penalties totalling Rs 88 lakh on the company and other individuals for various violations of securities market regulations. Further, the markets regulator directed Dabkara to take immediate steps to recoup the amount diverted from EKI Energy Services.
